title: Metaplectic groups, Weil representations and automorphic theta kernels
summary: Whole-roadmap pass over the metaplectic roadmap. It follows the two accepted parts, MetaplecticAutomorphicForms--MP.0 (layers MP.0–MP.7, 176 targets) and MetaplecticAutomorphicForms--MP.8 (85 targets), and adds the five targets the pass found missing. Four complete RT-AREA-automorphic-1/20 in MP.6: the metaplectic modular group Mp(2,ℤ) with vector-valued forms of half-integral weight, classical Jacobi forms of lattice index with their theta decomposition (Skoruppa), the unitary analogue of the Jacobi group with its Schrödinger–Weil representation, and the theta-paired Fourier–Jacobi coefficients along Heisenberg parabolics (Gan–Gross–Prasad). The fifth is the product formula and nonvanishing of the Jacobi theta function (MP.7), moved down from QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.1, which imports MP.7. Restructure R1–R6 route verified edits to the parts: a dependency order for the nine layers (eight targets change layer, after which no prerequisite runs backwards), exact suppliers for the local Langlands, Jacquet–Langlands and newform inputs that cited whole stages of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions and GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer, the removal of latent cycles with ML.4 and with QSeries, node ids for the sixteen bare stage citations inside MP.8, and the corrected Gaussian norm √det Y/(4a) of the genus-two theta series (BFH Proposition 2.1 prints 2a; source issue E-WR-1), with a check that the unfolding prefactor 1/(2mN³) does not depend on it. R7–R8 are proposals for the maintainer (the function-field programme; the overlap with the upstream Theta Series roadmap). Every routed item of the maintainer's fifteen added sources is planned by an accepted MP.0 target, and the five red-team findings are handled in the parts and here. The atlas builds the roadmap from all three packets; a dry assembly gives 266 declarations, 48 planets and no skipped links. All nine stages are planned in the sense of Protocol §0, with the parts' recorded gaps and requests retained. Complete describes this planning pass, not independent acceptance or mathematical closure.

nodes.title: The metaplectic modular group and vector-valued forms of half-integral weight
nodes.statement: Mp(2,ℤ) is the group of pairs (A, w) with A = [a, b; c, d] ∈ SL(2,ℤ) and w a holomorphic function on the upper half plane with w(τ)² = cτ + d, under (A, w)(B, v) = (AB, τ ↦ w(Bτ) v(τ)). The projection (A, w) ↦ A is surjective with kernel {(1, 1), (1, −1)}, which is central. For k ∈ ½ℤ the weight-k slash operator (f|_k(A, w))(τ) = w(τ)^{−2k} f(Aτ) is a right action of Mp(2,ℤ) on functions on the upper half plane, and (1, −1) acts by (−1)^{2k}. For a subgroup Γ ⊂ Mp(2,ℤ) of finite index and a finite-dimensional unitary representation ρ of Γ on V, a modular form of weight k and type (Γ, ρ) is a holomorphic f : ℍ → V with f|_k α = ρ(α) f for all α ∈ Γ such that, for every α ∈ Mp(2,ℤ), f|_k α has an expansion Σ c(l) q^l (q^l = e(lτ)) over real l ≥ 0 lying in finitely many cosets of (1/h)ℤ, h the width of the cusp α∞; cusp forms have l > 0 only, and weakly holomorphic forms allow finitely many l < 0. One-dimensional ρ are the multiplier systems. Mp(2,ℤ) is the preimage of SL(2,ℤ) in the real metaplectic double cover of MP.2 (MP.1/metaplectic-double-cover before restructure R1), the pair (A, w) corresponding to the lift whose weight-1/2 automorphy factor is w.
hypotheses: w ranges over holomorphic square roots of cτ + d on the simply connected upper half plane; there are exactly two for each A.

Expansions at the cusps are taken after slashing by every α ∈ Mp(2,ℤ), so the growth condition is imposed at every cusp. ρ is unitary, so ρ restricted to the stabilizer of a cusp is diagonalizable with eigenvalues e(κ_j), and the exponents lie in the cosets κ_j/h + (1/h)ℤ; they are rational when ρ has finite image, which the theta decomposition of MP.6/classical-jacobi-forms assumes. Non-unitary types, whose expansions acquire logarithmic terms, are not covered.
proofSteps: The composition is well defined and associative because the factors compose as automorphy factors: (w(Bτ)v(τ))² = (c(Bτ) + d)(c_Bτ + d_B), which is the bottom-row factor of AB at τ. The identity is (1, 1) and the inverse of (A, w) is (A⁻¹, τ ↦ 1/w(A⁻¹τ)).

Two square roots of the same nowhere-vanishing holomorphic function on a connected domain differ by a constant sign, so the kernel of the projection is {(1, ±1)}; it is central because constants commute with the composition.
The slash law (f|_kα)|_kβ = f|_k(αβ) is the composition rule raised to the power −2k; at α = (1, −1) the factor is (−1)^{−2k} = (−1)^{2k}.

Comparison with the real double cover: the lifts of SL(2,ℝ) acting on the weight-1/2 automorphy factor form the classical model of the double cover; MP.8/similitude-cover makes the same comparison in genus two. Restricting to SL(2,ℤ) gives Mp(2,ℤ). The comparison is made on generators and preserves the central sign.
acceptance: S̃ = (S, √τ) with the principal root and T̃ = (T, 1) satisfy S̃² = (−1, i) = (S̃T̃)³ and S̃⁴ = (1, −1), so S̃ has order 8.
For integral k and ρ trivial on (1, −1) the forms of type (Γ, ρ) are the classical vector-valued forms on the image of Γ in SL(2,ℤ).

nodes.title: Unitary Jacobi group and its Schrödinger–Weil representation
nodes.statement: Let k/k₀ be a quadratic extension of local fields of characteristic zero, or the split algebra k₀ × k₀, with involution σ and quadratic character ω_{k/k₀}. Let (W, ⟨ , ⟩) be a nondegenerate skew-Hermitian k-space and let W₀ be W regarded as a k₀-space with the symplectic form Tr_{k/k₀}⟨ , ⟩. Then U(W) ⊂ Sp(W₀), and U(W) acts on the Heisenberg group H(W₀) = W₀ × k₀ of MP.0 by isometries of W₀, fixing the centre. The unitary Jacobi group is the semidirect product J_U(W) = H(W₀) ⋊ U(W). For a nontrivial unitary character ψ of k₀ and a character µ of k^× with µ|_{k₀^×} = ω_{k/k₀}, the splitting s_{ψ,µ} : U(W) → S_ψ into the scalar metaplectic extension of MP.1 (MP.3/unitary-splitting, for the dual pair formed by W and the Hermitian line of discriminant 1) gives a linear representation ω_{ψ,µ}(h, g) = ρ_ψ(h) A_{s_{ψ,µ}(g)} of J_U(W) on the smooth Schrödinger model, where A_s is the unitary operator component of s ∈ S_ψ. Its restriction to H(W₀) is the Stone–von Neumann representation with central character ψ, and its restriction to U(W) is the Weil representation ω_{ψ,µ}. Over a quadratic extension E/F of number fields, with ψ a character of 𝔸/F and µ a character of 𝔸_E^×/E^× restricting to ω_{E/F} on 𝔸^×, the local representations assemble into the restricted tensor product representation of J_U(W)(𝔸) on S(Y(𝔸)) for a Lagrangian Y ⊂ W₀, and Weil's theta distribution φ ↦ Σ_{ξ∈Y(F)} (ω_{ψ,µ}(j)φ)(ξ) is an automorphic realization θ_{ψ,µ} of it on J_U(W)(F)\J_U(W)(𝔸), with central character ψ.
hypotheses: Characteristic zero; W nondegenerate skew-Hermitian over k, of any dimension (W = 0 allowed); ψ nontrivial; µ|_{k₀^×} = ω_{k/k₀} exactly. The auxiliary Hermitian space is the line of discriminant 1, so the restriction condition has exponent 1, not dim W.

The symplectic form on W₀ is Tr_{k/k₀}⟨ , ⟩, as for V₁ ⊗ W with V₁ the Hermitian line of discriminant 1. Rescaling the form rescales ψ by the same factor, and the rescaling must be transported, not ignored.

Globally the local splittings are the standard ones at almost all places (where W₀ has a self-dual lattice stable under the integral unitary group and ψ, µ are unramified), so that their restricted product is defined.
proofSteps: U(W) preserves Tr_{k/k₀}⟨ , ⟩, so it embeds in Sp(W₀); its action on H(W₀) is the restriction of MP.0/isometry-action and fixes the centre.
Form the semidirect product with Mathlib's SemidirectProduct; the multiplication is (h, g)(h′, g′) = (h · (g · h′), gg′).

The covariance A_s ρ_ψ(h) A_s⁻¹ = ρ_ψ(g · h) for s = s_{ψ,µ}(g), which is the defining property of S_ψ (MP.1/scalar-normalizer-extension), shows that (h, g) ↦ ρ_ψ(h) A_{s_{ψ,µ}(g)} is multiplicative; it is linear, not projective, because s_{ψ,µ} is a homomorphism into S_ψ.

Globally, at almost all places the local splitting fixes the standard lattice vector, so the restricted tensor product of the local representations is defined (MP.4/adelic-weil-representation). For γ in U(W)(F) the product over all places of the local splittings agrees with the canonical rational splitting of MP.4/rational-symplectic-splitting, because µ is trivial on E^× and the Weil indices satisfy the product formula (MP.4/global-weil-index-product). The theta distribution is invariant under the rationally split Sp(W₀)(F) (MP.5/theta-kernel) and under the rational points of H(W₀) (Poisson summation along Y), hence under J_U(W)(F).

Degenerate cases: if W = 0 the group is the centre k₀ and ω_{ψ,µ} = ψ, with no dependence on µ; if k = k₀ × k₀, U(W) is a general linear group of a polarization of W₀ and the splitting is the standard linear one.
acceptance: For W = 0, J_U(W) is the centre k₀ and ω_{ψ,µ} is the character ψ.
For dim_k W = 1, W₀ is a symplectic plane and U(W) = k¹ = {z : zσ(z) = 1} acts on it as an anisotropic torus of SL₂(k₀); for k = ℂ, k₀ = ℝ it is the maximal compact subgroup SO(2) of SL₂(ℝ).

nodes.title: Fourier–Jacobi coefficients along Heisenberg parabolics, symplectic and unitary
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field and let W ⊂ V be nondegenerate spaces over E of one of the two Fourier–Jacobi types: both symplectic (E = F), or both skew-Hermitian for a quadratic extension E/F. Assume W^⊥ = X ⊕ X^∨ with X, X^∨ isotropic and in duality, dim_E X = n ≥ 0. Let H = N ⋊ G(W) ⊂ G(V) be the subgroup attached to a full isotropic flag in X: N is the unipotent radical of the parabolic stabilizing the flag, λ the G(W)-invariant generic character of N, and N → H(W₀) the G(W)-equivariant homomorphism to the Heisenberg group of W₀ (W over F with the form 2⟨ , ⟩ in the symplectic case and Tr_{E/F}⟨ , ⟩ in the skew-Hermitian case). Through MP.6/jacobi-group (symplectic case, on the metaplectic cover of Sp(W)) or MP.6/unitary-jacobi-group and a character µ (skew-Hermitian case), the theta functions θ(φ), φ ∈ S(Y(𝔸)), pull back to H(F)\H(𝔸); put θ_ν(φ) = θ(φ) · λ. For a cuspidal automorphic form f on G(V)(𝔸) (and, in the symplectic case, the appropriate cover), the Fourier–Jacobi coefficient is FJ(f, φ)(g) = ∫_{N(F)\N(𝔸)} f(ng) θ_ν(φ)(ng) dn for g in G(W)(𝔸) (its metaplectic cover in the symplectic case), and the Fourier–Jacobi period of f ⊗ f′ ⊗ φ, for f′ an automorphic form on G(W) (a genuine form on the metaplectic cover of Sp(W) in the symplectic case, so that f′ · θ_ν(φ) descends), is 𝒫(f, f′, φ) = ∫_{H(F)\H(𝔸)} f(h) f′(h) θ_ν(φ)(h) dh. FJ(f, φ) is left G(W)(F)-invariant and rapidly decreasing, the period converges absolutely, and 𝒫(f, f′, φ) = ∫_{G(W)(F)\G(W)(𝔸)} FJ(f, φ)(g) f′(g) dg.
hypotheses: Fourier–Jacobi type in the sense of GGP §§12 and 23: V and W both symplectic, or both skew-Hermitian, with W^⊥ split of even dimension 2n; n = 0 is allowed (then N = 1 and H = G(W) = G(V)).

f is a smooth cusp form; f′ is of moderate growth; the measure on N(F)\N(𝔸) is the probability measure and the measure on G(W)(F)\G(W)(𝔸) is fixed in advance. In the skew-Hermitian case µ is an automorphic character of 𝔸_E^× with µ|_{𝔸^×} = ω_{E/F}.

The pairing convention is GGP's (f · θ, no complex conjugate). Sources that pair with the conjugate theta function use the data (ψ⁻¹, µ⁻¹), since complex conjugation carries ω_{ψ,µ} to ω_{ψ⁻¹,µ⁻¹} (MP.2/character-and-dual); the two conventions must not be mixed.
proofSteps: GGP §12 constructs, for n ≥ 1, the G(W)-equivariant homomorphism from N to H(W₀) and the generic character λ; with the Jacobi group of MP.6/jacobi-group, or MP.6/unitary-jacobi-group and µ, this gives a homomorphism from H to the Jacobi group (on the metaplectic cover in the symplectic case).
Pull back Weil's theta functions (MP.5/theta-kernel, MP.6/unitary-jacobi-group) and multiply by λ; the result is smooth and of uniform moderate growth on H(F)\H(𝔸) (MP.5/theta-growth-transfer).

N(F)\N(𝔸) is compact (AF.3/unipotent-quotient-compact), so FJ(f, φ) is defined; left G(W)(F)-invariance follows from the invariance of f and of θ_ν under H(F). A cusp form is rapidly decreasing (AF.3/cusp-form-rapid-decay), which dominates the moderate growth of θ_ν and f′; hence the period converges absolutely and Fubini over N gives the stated equality.
Equivariance: replacing (f, f′, φ) by their translates under h′ ∈ H(𝔸) through R(h′), R(h′) and ν(h′) leaves 𝒫 unchanged; FJ(R(g′)f, ω(g′)φ)(g) = FJ(f, φ)(g g′) for g′ in G(W)(𝔸).

Integrating first over the centre of the Heisenberg group against ψ⁻¹ isolates the ψ-isotypic part of f, the central Fourier–Jacobi coefficient of MP.6/fourier-jacobi-extraction; FJ pairs that part with θ_ν(φ).

Degenerate cases: if W = 0, ν is a generic character of the unipotent radical of a Borel subgroup and FJ is the corresponding Whittaker coefficient (MP.5/metaplectic-constant-and-whittaker); if n = 0, FJ(f, φ) = f · θ(φ) on G(W) = G(V).
acceptance: W = 0 recovers the Whittaker coefficient of f for a generic character; n = 0 recovers the equal-rank pairing ∫ f f′ θ(φ).

nodes.title: Classical Jacobi forms of lattice index and their theta decomposition
nodes.statement: Let F be a symmetric positive definite half-integral n × n matrix (2F integral with even diagonal) and F[x] = xᵗFx. For a subgroup Γ ⊂ Mp(2,ℤ) of finite index, J_n(Γ) = Γ ⋉ (ℤⁿ × ℤⁿ), with (α, (λ, µ))(α′, (λ′, µ′)) = (αα′, (λ, µ)A′ + (λ′, µ′)) and (λ, µ)A = (aλ + cµ, bλ + dµ) for A = [a, b; c, d] the image of α′. For k ∈ ½ℤ, J_n(Γ) acts on the right on functions on ℍ × ℂⁿ by φ|_{k,F}(A, w)(τ, z) = w(τ)^{−2k} e(−c F[z]/(cτ + d)) φ(Aτ, z/(cτ + d)) and φ|_{k,F}[λ, µ](τ, z) = e(τ F[λ] + 2zᵗFλ) φ(τ, z + λτ + µ). A Jacobi form of weight k, index F and type (Γ, ρ), for a finite-dimensional representation ρ of Γ on V, is a holomorphic φ : ℍ × ℂⁿ → V with φ|_{k,F} g = ρ(g)φ for g ∈ J_n(Γ) (ℤⁿ × ℤⁿ acting trivially on V) such that, for every α ∈ Mp(2,ℤ), φ|_{k,F}α = Σ c(l, r) q^l e(zᵗr) over l ∈ ℚ and r ∈ ℤⁿ with 4l − F⁻¹[r] ≥ 0; cusp forms have 4l − F⁻¹[r] > 0. With the theta functions ϑ_{F,x}(τ, z) = Σ_{r ≡ x mod 2Fℤⁿ} e(τ F⁻¹[r]/4 + rᵗz), every Jacobi form is uniquely Σ_{x ∈ ℤⁿ/2Fℤⁿ} h_x(τ) ϑ_{F,x}(τ, z), and when ρ has finite image the map φ ↦ (h_x) is an isomorphism J_{k,F}(Γ, ρ) ≅ (M_{k−n/2} ⊗ W(F)^*) ⊗_{ℂ[Mp(2,ℤ)]} Ind ρ. Here W(F) is the Weil representation of Mp(2,ℤ) on ℂ[ℤⁿ/2Fℤⁿ] for the quadratic form x ↦ F⁻¹[x]/4 mod ℤ; it is ρ_{L_F} for the even lattice L_F = (ℤⁿ, 2F) and the complex conjugate of the representation ω_{L_F} of MP.4/finite-weil-representation. Consequently J_{k,F}(Γ, ρ) = 0 for k < n/2, and J_{n/2,F}(Γ, ρ) ≅ Hom_{Mp(2,ℤ)}(W(F), Ind ρ).
hypotheses: F positive definite and half-integral in the even-diagonal sense; a half-integral scalar index such as 1/2 is not covered and is reached by rescaling z (ϑ(τ, 2z) has index 2).
k ∈ ½ℤ; for k ∉ ℤ the slash operator uses the Mp(2,ℤ) factor w(τ)^{−2k}; the decomposition theorem needs ρ of finite image (so that the components are modular forms on a subgroup of finite index).
W(F) is normalized by (T, 1)e_x = e(F⁻¹[x]/4)e_x and (S, √τ)e_x = σ|D_F|^{−1/2} Σ_y e(−B(y, x)) e_y with σ = |D_F|^{−1/2} Σ_x e(−F⁻¹[x]/4) = e(−n/8) (Milgram).
proofSteps: The group law and the right action are checked on generators. Composing [λ, µ] and then [λ′, µ′] gives [λ + λ′, µ + µ′] up to the phase e(2µ′ᵗFλ) = e(µ′ᵗ(2F)λ), which is 1 because 2F is integral; this is why the integral Jacobi group needs no central coordinate.

Invariance under ℤⁿ × ℤⁿ makes the coefficients c(l, r) depend only on 4l − F⁻¹[r] and on r mod 2Fℤⁿ, which groups the expansion into Σ_x h_x ϑ_{F,x}; uniqueness is the linear independence of the ϑ_{F,x} (their orthogonality, the n-variable form of the Gaussian pairing of MP.8/theta-pairing and of MP.6/jacobi-theta-decomposition-interface).

The span Θ(F) of the ϑ_{F,x} is stable under |_{n/2,F} and is isomorphic to W(F)^* by λ ↦ Σ λ(x)ϑ_{F,x} (Poisson summation gives the S-transformation); the components h_x therefore form a vector-valued form of weight k − n/2 for W(F)^* ⊗ Ind ρ, and the cusp conditions match.

W(F) = ρ_{L_F}: the discriminant module of L_F = (ℤⁿ, 2F) is (2F)⁻¹ℤⁿ/ℤⁿ ≅ ℤⁿ/2Fℤⁿ with q(y) = yᵗFy = F⁻¹[x]/4 for y = (2F)⁻¹x; complex conjugation of ω_{L_F} is recorded on MP.4/finite-weil-representation.
Weight k < n/2 leaves M_{k−n/2} = 0; at k = n/2 the constants give the Hom description.
acceptance: For n = 1, F = (m), k ∈ ℤ, Γ = SL(2,ℤ) and ρ trivial, the definition is Eichler–Zagier's J_{k,m}, and ϑ_{m,x} are their theta functions Σ_{r ≡ x (2m)} q^{r²/4m} ζ^r.
For F = (1), σ(D_1) = 2^{−1/2}(1 + e(−1/4)) = e(−1/8), matching Milgram's formula with signature 1.

nodes.title: Product formula and nonvanishing of the Jacobi theta function
nodes.statement: For τ in the upper half plane put w = exp(πiτ), so that |w| < 1. Then Mathlib's jacobiTheta τ = Σ_{n∈ℤ} exp(πin²τ) equals the absolutely convergent product ∏_{n≥1}(1 − w^{2n})(1 + w^{2n−1})². No factor vanishes, so jacobiTheta τ ≠ 0 for every τ with Im τ > 0. Consequently the theta series θ(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ} e(n²z) = jacobiTheta(2z) of MP.7 has no zero on the upper half plane, and neither has the unitary normalization y^{1/4}θ(z), y = Im z.
hypotheses: τ ∈ ℂ with Im τ > 0; e(x) = exp(2πix). No square root or other branch enters the statement.
The product is over n ≥ 1 and converges absolutely because Σ_n |w|^n < ∞; the identity is an identity of complex numbers, not only of formal power series.
proofSteps: Formal identity. ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.4/theta-product-specialisations, part (ii), gives Σ_{n∈ℤ} x^{n²} = ∏_{n≥1}(1 + x^{2n−1})²(1 − x^{2n}) in ℤ⟦x⟧ with the pi topology. Equivalently, for each j the coefficient of x^j in the finite products over n ≤ M is eventually (for M large) the number of n ∈ ℤ with n² = j.

Analytic identity. On the open unit disc the finite products converge locally uniformly to the infinite product, since Σ_n (2|x|^{2n−1} + |x|^{4n−2} + |x|^{2n}) converges locally uniformly there. A locally uniform limit of holomorphic functions is holomorphic, and its Taylor coefficients at 0 are the limits of the coefficients (Cauchy estimates); by the first step they are the coefficients of Σ x^{n²}, which is holomorphic on the disc. Two holomorphic functions on the disc with the same power series at 0 coincide (uniqueness of power series, HasFPowerSeriesAt.eq_formalMultilinearSeries, and the identity theorem on the connected disc). Kong–Teo prove the same analytic identity directly by a two-variable argument (Theorem 3.1); either proof may be used.
Substitute x = w = exp(πiτ): the defining series of jacobiTheta is Σ_n w^{n²}. jacobiTheta_eq_jacobiTheta₂ identifies it with jacobiTheta₂ 0 τ when the two-variable form is preferred.

Nonvanishing. Write the product as ∏_i (1 + f_i) over the interleaved family f = (−w^{2n}, w^{2n−1}, w^{2n−1})_{n≥1}. Each 1 + f_i is nonzero because |f_i| < 1, and Σ_i |f_i| < ∞; tprod_one_add_ne_zero_of_summable gives a nonzero product.
θ(z) = Σ_n exp(2πi n² z) = Σ_n exp(πi n² (2z)) = jacobiTheta(2z), and 2z lies in the upper half plane when z does; y^{1/4} > 0.
acceptance: At τ = i: jacobiTheta i = π^{1/4}/Γ(3/4) ≈ 1.0864, and the product truncated at n = 2 agrees with it to three decimal places.

Consistency with Mathlib: norm_jacobiTheta_sub_one_le gives ‖jacobiTheta τ − 1‖ < 1, hence nonvanishing, only where exp(−π Im τ) < 1/3. The theorem covers the whole half plane, including the region near the cusp τ = 1, where jacobiTheta tends to 0 and no such bound can apply.

Non-example: the two-variable function vanishes, jacobiTheta₂ ((1 + τ)/2) τ = 0, because the factor with n = 1 of the two-variable triple product vanishes there. Nonvanishing is special to the specialisation z = 0.

sourceIssues.printed: The integral of θ^{N₀}_ν(Z, W) times the conjugate of θ^{N₀}_μ(Z, W) times exp(−4πN₀ Y⁻¹[Im W]) over ℂ²/Λ_Z, against Lebesgue measure, is stated to be √det Y/(2N₀) when μ ≡ ν mod 2N₀.
sourceIssues.reason: Write W = Zλ + ρ; then dW = det(Y) dλ dρ on [0, 1)⁴. Integrating in ρ leaves the diagonal R = R′; the exponent is −4πN₀·Y[λ + R/(2N₀)]; summing over R ≡ ν mod 2N₀ and λ ∈ [0, 1)² gives ∫_{ℝ²} exp(−4πN₀ Y[u]) du = 1/(4N₀ √det Y), and multiplying by det Y gives √det Y/(4N₀). In one variable the same computation gives Eichler–Zagier's √(v/4m), and for Y = vI₂ the two-variable value is its square, v/(4N₀).

Why it affects nothing in BFH: Proposition 2.2 obtains the theta components from Fourier coefficients ((2.5)–(2.6), (2.10)–(2.11)); Proposition 2.1 is invoked once, on p. 554, to deduce (2.7), and only its orthogonality is used there; the unfolding of §5 uses the Gaussian integral on p. 581.
